statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34181 (OpenSSL security advisory of 9 June 2026): PKCS#12 verification accepts a PBMAC1 integrity check whose HMAC key is as short as one byte, so a service that authenticates PKCS#12 files by password can be made to accept a forged certificate and private key with a 1 in 256 chance. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 fixes it; the FIPS modules are not affected. The fix on the openssl-3.5 branch is commit 85dcbb3, which makes crypto/pkcs12/p12_mutl.c reject PBMAC1 key lengths outside 20 to 64 bytes with the error text 'Invalid Key length (%d is not in the range 20..64)': https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/85dcbb3abaa4878af5c8fbbe11bce708fcf984a7. Checked the libcrypto3 package of every openssl build published for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, each against the index checksum. The libcrypto.so.3 version string is OpenSSL 3.5.4, 3.5.5 or 3.5.6 in 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0 and 3.5.6-r1, and OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later in 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2; the fix's error text is absent from libcrypto.so.3 in every build before 3.5.7-r0 and present in 3.5.7-r0 and every later build. So 3.5.7-r0 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-34181 (OpenSSL security advisory of 9 June 2026): PKCS#12 verification accepts a PBMAC1 integrity check whose HMAC key is as short as one byte, so a service that authenticates PKCS#12 files by password can be made to accept a forged certificate and private key with a 1 in 256 chance. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 fixes it; the FIPS modules are not affected. The fix on the openssl-3.5 branch is commit 85dcbb3, which makes crypto/pkcs12/p12_mutl.c reject PBMAC1 key lengths outside 20 to 64 bytes with the error text 'Invalid Key length (%d is not in the range 20..64)': https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/85dcbb3abaa4878af5c8fbbe11bce708fcf984a7. Debian fixed it in trixie in 3.5.6-1~deb13u2: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-34181. Every DHI Debian 13 openssl build is built from Debian's trixie source. Checked the libssl3t64 package, which holds libcrypto.so.3, of every published build for amd64 and arm64, each against the index SHA256: the builds from 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, including their +fips builds, carry no changelog entry for this CVE and lack the fix's error text in libcrypto.so.3, and every build from 3.5.6-1~deb13u2+dhi0 on, through 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and including their +fips builds, lists the CVE in its changelog and has the fix's error text in libcrypto.so.3. The +fips builds compile libcrypto.so.3 from the same Debian source, and their FIPS provider is outside the affected code. So 3.5.6-1~deb13u2+dhi0 is the first fixed build.
